mechanism_fit: This is M10 (entry-point blame). The trigger calls only the public entry NaturalRanking.rank(double[]). That method has visible validation (the FAILED strategy throws NotANumberException) and visible branching (a switch over MAXIMAL, MINIMAL, REMOVED, FIXED and FAILED, plus the tie-walk loop). The fault is in the private guard containsNaNs, two calls below the entry under REMOVED (rank -> removeNaNs -> containsNaNs) and one call below under FAILED. The symptom is that the result has one extra rank (length 6 instead of 5). That fits the entry's REMOVED branch and its output sizing, and it fits removeNaNs, whose nested loop that shifts positions looks error-prone. The failure is an assertion in the test, not an exception, so no stack frame points below the entry. The entry is listed in entry_points, not in decoys, so a run that ranks it first is counted as ENTRY_POINT, as in sibling specs.
gold: org.apache.commons.math3.stat.ranking.NaturalRanking::containsNaNs (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/stat/ranking/NaturalRanking.java). The loop bound changes from i < ranks.length to i < ranks.length - 1, so a NaN that is the only NaN and sits in the last position is reported as absent. The minimal repair restores i < ranks.length.
ownership_reason: The javadoc of containsNaNs says it returns 'true iff ranks contains one or more NaNs'. The variant breaks that contract, because its scan stops before the last index. removeNaNs is correct with respect to that contract: its own removal pass visits every index. The passing test NaturalRankingTest.testNaNsRemovedTiesSequential shows it dropping NaNs at interior and trailing positions with correct position shifts (exampleData has a NaN at index 6 of 9; multipleNaNs has NaNs at indices 2 and 3). rank() sends each NaNStrategy to the helper for that role. It is pinned by testDefault and testNaNsFailed (FAILED throws for an interior NaN) and by the REMOVED test. Its FAILED branch was changed only by a context edit that G1 proved behaviour-preserving. The sibling scans getNanPositions and recodeNaNs in the same class both loop over i < ranks.length. The trigger needs both production callers of containsNaNs to detect the trailing NaN: REMOVED must drop it and FAILED must throw. So no edit limited to removeNaNs or to rank() repairs it, and G9 confirms this for the declared edits, including the edit that bypasses the guard in removeNaNs. Ownership tests: testNaNsRemovedTiesSequential, testNaNsFailed and testDefault. All three pass on both the CORRECT configuration and the variant.
trigger: The test org.apache.commons.math3.stat.ranking.NaturalRankingTest::testNaNsRemovedThenFailed (JUnit4, same style as the file). It uses data = {8, 3, 5, 3, 9, Double.NaN}. First, new NaturalRanking(NaNStrategy.REMOVED).rank(data) must equal {4, 1.5, 3, 1.5, 5}, checked with TestUtils.assertEquals(correctRanks, ranks, 0d). Second, new NaturalRanking(NaNStrategy.FAILED).rank(data) must throw NotANumberException. Only public behaviour is observed.
